newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian sugar prices rise helped by thin supply.
newsitem.headline: Indian sugar prices rise helped by thin supply.

text.p: Indian sugar prices gained on Thursday helped by thin supplies and a shortage of ready stock, dealers said.

Ready delivery sugar S-30 rose by 4/5 rupees to 1,255/1,295 rupees per quintal while M-30 gained by five rupees to 1,300/1,380 rupees. Arrivals remained low due to few offerings by mill owners on account of low free sale quota for January which is 650,000 tonnes against 800,000 tonnes in December.
Sugar mill delivery fell by 15 rupees to 1,200/1,215 rupees as outstation mill demand eased at higher levels.
